findings.title: L1 diagnostic event failures are consumed without recording or reporting
findings.scenario: Inside the exit runner window, cudaEventCreateWithFlags, cudaEventRecord, cudaEventQuery or cudaEventDestroy fails once with a non-sticky error; the later cudaStreamSynchronize succeeds. The diagnostic helper clears the error with cudaGetLastError and stores no FailureRecord, so synchronize returns success and the exit log contains no CUDA failure. Create/record failure also falls straight through to a potentially unbounded silent stream wait, contradicting L1 a3. After a query error following a diagnostic it can print that the work finished although completion was not proved by the query.
findings.fix: Record every failed diagnostic event call before consuming its slot, with call/purpose/device tags, and route it through the existing raise-once/exit logger. Provide a diagnosed fallback when the marker cannot be created/recorded; print completion only on success.
findings.evidence: CPU actual-source host trace: logs/p1t_rev8_diagnostic_errors.log, four one-shot call failures erased (error=null, slot=0); no GPU run.
findings.prior_art: NVIDIA CUDA 12.6 Runtime API event/error-slot contracts (2024); FIX5 V5-02 record-before-consume. Standard contracts and existing error accounting reused; reviewer contribution is the exit-window failure census.

findings.title: Native exit loggers silently abandon recorded CUDA failures on reporting allocation failure
findings.scenario: The Python hook is interrupted, so its native runner is the last reporter. A CUDA failure is already recorded (for example the interrupted add-on runner synchronize drained with an error and could not allocate its message). report_message / unraisable_message or the core record snapshot then throws bad_alloc. The exit logger catches it and writes nothing. Keeping the record cannot recover it after interpreter exit: there is no next synchronize.
findings.fix: Provide an allocation-free stderr fallback that emits the existing tagged records, or at least the count and first failed call/device/error, when rich-message construction fails. Keep quiescence first and preserve the hook exception.
findings.evidence: Actual add-on source included and C++ allocation failures injected only inside exit_log_unreported: logs/p1t_rev8_exit_log_oom.log contains record_still_pending=True and no CUDA stderr; control logs/p1t_rev8_exit_log_control.log names cudaEventQuery and consumes record. Core identical silent catch confirmed by source reasoning; no GPU required. Core exact-source OOM/control now independently reproduced: logs/p1t_rev8_core_exit_oom_retry.log has no CUDA stderr, logs/p1t_rev8_core_exit_control_retry.log logs the recorded failure. Initial child had an invalid stats-key assertion; corrected before accepting evidence.
findings.prior_art: SQLite OOM fault-injection testing; C++17 bad_alloc; existing allocation-free FailureRecord/static core site string. Taken: fail allocations and report using pre-existing POD data; reviewer contribution is the last-reader-at-exit scenario.
